Subject: Immediate safeguard deployment — customer action and follow-up

Hi team,

We discovered a live KV-cache desynchronization on a small subset of Dedicated nodes that, under a particular model variant rollout, has produced token-duplication and a slow memory increase on recent requests. SREs are pushing a protective configuration now to stop further growth. This is an unscheduled, short-impact action; we want to give you the actions to take on your side and what to expect.

Impact (what we saw):
- Elevated duplicate token outputs and occasional 503s for long-running streaming sessions.
- Memory pressure on a subset of GPU hosts serving Dataware traffic (approx. 8% of your dedicated pool).

Immediate customer ask (please apply these ASAP):
1) Restart long-lived streaming clients or reconnect sessions where possible (see client_restart_snippets.txt attached). A reconnect will flush the server-side prefix cache for the session.
2) Add a short client-side exponential backoff for 429/503 with max 30s; this avoids request storms during the rollback window.
3) If you can, pin calls to model variant: rwv-v1-stable for the next 2 hours (we will remove the pin when safe).

What we are doing:
- Pushing a safeguard flag to disable the problematic prefix compacting optimizer and roll traffic to a safe kernel.
- Monitoring memory and error rates; we expect the change to complete within 30-45 minutes.
- Preparing a postmortem and remediation plan; draft will be shared after stabilization.

Attachments: safeguard_instructions_v1.pdf (server-side steps), client_restart_snippets.txt (client code samples).

Apologies for the short notice — I know this is disruptive. I will keep you updated every 15 minutes and share the postmortem once we have a full timeline. If you need an immediate call, reply with your availability and we’ll escalate to a bridge.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Quick technical update and what to expect during the safeguard deploy:
- Root cause (preliminary): an edge case in prefix compaction combined with a model sequence-length misreport during the rwv-v1 rollout. The compaction path can drop/duplicate certain kv entries under load.
- Short-term mitigation: flip the runtime flag that routes requests away from the compaction kernel to the stable path; this adds ~3-5ms p50 but removes the memory leak and duplication.
- Rollback: we can revert flag within 5 minutes if any regression is observed.

Monitoring plan:
- Watch rates for 503/err and memory usage per host (alerts at +15% from baseline).
- I’ll post the SRE dashboard link once the push begins.

Note: if you see any long-running streams terminate, a client reconnect is expected and safe. The attached server steps include the exact RPCs we call.

Ben
Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference

Update: Safeguard completed and verified at 11:45 PT.

Summary:
- What we changed: disabled prefix compaction kernel on the impacted shard set and routed traffic to the stable execution path.
- Impact: memory usage returned to baseline within ~8 minutes; error/duplicate-token rates dropped to nominal; there were brief reconnects for ~4% of active streams.
- Customer visible effect: brief reconnections and ~1-2 minute elevated latency for in-flight requests; no data loss.

Next steps and follow-up:
- We will share a full postmortem with timeline and root-cause analysis by EOD tomorrow (link: https://drive.redwood.com/links/safeguard-deploy-20280517).
- Draft postmortem attached (postmortem-draft.md). Your engineers are welcome to review and add notes.
- If Dataware would like a call to review the timeline and any SLA considerations, I can set a follow-up for tomorrow morning.
